records.context: Reads the merged arrays of ``translocation_merged_folder`` (or ``<src>/merged``). With ``cell_from_nucleus_expand_px`` above 0 a five-image layer array ``[c0, c1, c2, nucleus, parasite]`` gets its cell image layer from the nuclei first (:func:`nucleus_territories`) and becomes the six-image layer layout; a six-image layer array already has its cell image layer (Make Masks grows the territories itself with the same setting) and is read as it is. Cells are marked ``cell_source`` nucleus_territory when the territories were grown here or the merged folder's image layer layout says Make Masks grew them; the territories are not cell outlines. Then :func:`translocation_cells` per field and :func:`translocation_summary`, written to ``<src>/translocation/`` (cells_translocation.csv, the summary tables and the translocation_ratio_vs_vacuoles figure of :func:`translocation_figure`).
records.label: spacr.host_pathogen.nuclear_translocation#1
records.source: Reads the merged arrays of ``translocation_merged_folder`` (or ``<src>/merged``). With ``cell_from_nucleus_expand_px`` above 0 a five-plane array ``[c0, c1, c2, nucleus, parasite]`` gets its cell plane from the nuclei first (:func:`nucleus_territories`) and becomes the six-plane layout; a six-plane array already has its cell plane (Make Masks grows the territories itself with the same setting) and is read as it is. Cells are marked ``cell_source`` nucleus_territory when the territories were grown here or the merged folder's plane layout says Make Masks grew them; the territories are not cell outlines. Then :func:`translocation_cells` per field and :func:`translocation_summary`, written to ``<src>/translocation/`` (cells_translocation.csv, the summary tables and the translocation_ratio_vs_vacuoles figure of :func:`translocation_figure`).
records.translation: Lê os arrays mesclados de ``translocation_merged_folder`` (ou ``<src>/merged``). Com ``cell_from_nucleus_expand_px`` acima de 0, um array de cinco planos ``[c0, c1, c2, nucleus, parasite]`` recebe primeiro o seu plano de células a partir dos núcleos (:func:`nucleus_territories`) e passa ao layout de seis planos; um array de seis planos já tem o seu plano de células (Make Masks expande os territórios ele próprio com a mesma configuração) e é lido tal como está. As células são marcadas ``cell_source`` nucleus_territory quando os territórios foram expandidos aqui ou quando o layout de planos da pasta mesclada indica que Make Masks os expandiu; os territórios não são contornos de células. Depois, :func:`translocation_cells` por campo e :func:`translocation_summary`, gravados em ``<src>/translocation/`` (cells_translocation.csv, as tabelas de resumo e a figura translocation_ratio_vs_vacuoles de :func:`translocation_figure`).
